documentsNeeded: Approved Kenya Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA)
Passport valid for at least six months beyond your planned arrival date, with at least one blank page
Passport-type photo or selfie
Confirmed accommodation booking and onward/return travel itinerary

Kenyan Government travel health insurance (mandatory from 5 October 2026 for most visitors staying under 12 months): bought as part of the eTA application, or through the eCitizen insurance portal if you already hold an eTA; foreign travel insurance doesn't replace it. It is valid for 90 days, for multiple entries.
notes: Standard eTA fee is USD 30 for a single entry; the eTA itself is valid for travel within 90 days of issuance (you must enter Kenya within that window). The actual length of stay granted is set by the immigration officer at the point of entry (Kenya Citizenship and Immigration Regulations, 2012, reg. 30(3): a visitor's pass is capped at 6 months from the date of entry, at the officer's discretion) — there is no single published guaranteed number of days for eTA holders, so no fixed maxDays is shown here. American nationals also have the option of a Five-Year Multi-Entry eTA (USD 185) in addition to the Standard single-entry eTA (USD 30).

notes: American passport holders are on the Egypt e-Visa Portal's own list of nationalities eligible to apply for an e-Visa (the FAQ page states "a visa is required prior to entry into The Arab Republic of Egypt" and that eligible nationals "may be issued with an e-Visa upon application on the Egypt e-Visa Portal" — this is legally a visa, issued entirely online without an embassy visit, not a lighter-weight travel authorisation, so it is modeled here as visa_required rather than eta_required). The e-Visa portal does not publish a specific permitted-stay length (number of days) anywhere in its publicly reachable FAQ, About, How-to-Apply, Disclaimer or Terms pages — the commonly repeated "30 days" figure on travel-blog and visa-agency sites was not confirmed against this or any other primary Egyptian government source in this pass, so no fixed maxDays is published (stayPolicy stays at visa_required / no computable duration) rather than guessed. The e-Visa is not available to holders of Diplomatic, Service, Special, Official, Temporary, Nansen, Refugee, Mission, Alien's, or July-51-Agreement passports — those travelers must apply at an Egyptian embassy or consulate instead.

documentsNeeded: Approved Nigeria e-Visa (Tourism Visa – F5A) obtained online before travel, or an embassy-issued visa
Passport valid for at least 6 months
Passport-size photo
Evidence of return ticket
Evidence of hotel reservation or host address in Nigeria
Evidence of sufficient funds (180-day bank statement)
notes: The Nigeria Immigration Service states the Tourism Visa (F5A) is for "citizens of all countries except ECOWAS member States and other countries which Nigeria has entered into visa abolition/waiver agreements". The United States is not an ECOWAS member, and no primary source found in this pass names it as having a visa-waiver agreement with Nigeria for ordinary passports (NIS publishes no such list). F5A terms (checked 2026-10-19): validity 90 days from issuance, single entry, stay of 30 days, not extendable, no employment. Fees were not verified — confirm on the official e-Visa portal (evisa.immigration.gov.ng).

legal_source.name: Nigeria Immigration Service — Tourism Visa (F5A)

documentsNeeded: Approved Nigeria e-Visa (Tourism Visa – F5A) obtained online before travel, or an embassy-issued Short Visit Visa
Passport valid for at least 6 months from date of travel, with blank pages
Passport-size photo
Evidence of return/onward ticket
Evidence of hotel reservation or host address in Nigeria
Evidence of sufficient funds (180-day bank statement)
notes: Nigeria discontinued Visa on Arrival for eligible travellers effective 1 May 2025, replacing it with a mandatory online e-Visa system administered by the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS); only ECOWAS member-state nationals and a small number of countries with a separate visa-abolition/waiver agreement (e.g. Cameroon, Chad) are visa-exempt — no primary source found placing any of the 15-nationality roster in that exempt group. The Tourism Visa (F5A) is single-entry, valid for 90 days from issuance (you must enter Nigeria within that window), and grants a 30-day stay that cannot be extended — plan any longer trip around this hard limit; no employment is permitted. Applicants must also complete a digital Landing Card online before boarding (lecard.immigration.gov.ng). Visa fees vary by nationality and visa category and were not independently verified in this pass — confirm the current fee on the official e-Visa portal (evisa.immigration.gov.ng) before applying.

documentsNeeded: Approved Morocco eVisa (Autorisation Électronique de Voyage, applied for online via acces-maroc.ma) or a consular visa
Valid passport
Supporting documents for the eVisa application (confirmed travel itinerary, accommodation, proof of means)
notes: Israel does not appear on Morocco's visa-exemption list (consulat.ma) and Israeli passport holders require a visa to enter Morocco. Since 10 July 2022, Israeli nationals are one of the first two nationalities (with Thailand) named by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs as eligible for the "eVisa" fast-track via acces-maroc.ma instead of an in-person consulate visit — processed within 24h (express) or 72h (standard); the eVisa is a one-time authorization valid for up to 180 days from issue, within which it allows a stay of up to 30 days. This is based on a 2022 Ministry press release; current (2026) secondary sources describe the same 30-day/180-day terms, but given how diplomatically sensitive Morocco–Israel entry policy can be, re-confirm immediately before travel rather than relying solely on this record. A standard consular visa application remains the fallback route if eVisa eligibility has changed.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport with at least 6 months validity from the date of application
Approved e-Tourist Visa / Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA), applied for online at indianvisaonline.gov.in at least 4 days before arrival
Return or onward journey ticket
Proof of sufficient funds for the stay
Recent passport-style photograph (uploaded with the online application)
notes: India's e-Tourist Visa (e-T1 V) is issued as an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA): duration "One Month (30 Days)" from the date of first arrival, multiple entries permitted within that window, non-extendable and non-convertible. Longer 1-year and 5-year e-Tourist Visa options also exist (multiple entries), but both cap total stay at 180 days per calendar year rather than granting a longer single visit — this row reflects the standard 30-day option. Applicants must hold a passport valid at least 6 months from the date of application and show a return/onward ticket and sufficient funds; apply online at least 4 days before arrival. Diplomatic/official passport holders, and applicants of Pakistani origin or holding a Pakistani passport, are not eligible for any e-Visa category.

documentsNeeded: Valid New Zealand passport
notes: Special Category visa (subclass 444): granted automatically on arrival at no cost under the Trans-Tasman Travel Arrangement, no advance application needed. It has no fixed day-cap — Home Affairs describes the stay as lasting “from the time you are granted the visa until you leave Australia”, for as long as the holder remains a New Zealand citizen; it ceases on departure and a new SCV is granted on each re-entry. stayPolicy uses the non-computable placeholder because no numeric maxDays exists for this visa (same pattern used for Kenya's eTA), not because a visa application is required in advance.

legal_source.name: Department of Home Affairs — Special Category visa (subclass 444)

Visitor visa (subclass 600) application via ImmiAccount

documentsNeeded: Valid passport
Boarding card

Useful at the border if asked: travel itinerary, proof of sufficient funds, health/travel insurance covering your stay, accommodation details, and any invitation or letter explaining the purpose of your visit
notes: US nationals are on Ireland's non-visa-required list (official INIS table), so no visa or pre-clearance is needed to visit. Ireland has no ETA-style pre-travel authorisation. On arrival by air or sea from outside the State you must present to an Immigration Officer, who decides how long you may stay — INIS: "up to a maximum of 3 months" — and stamps your passport; the officer can still refuse entry if not satisfied by your documents or explanations. Staying beyond 90 days requires applying to Immigration Service Delivery for permission. Ireland is not in Schengen: days here do not count toward the 90/180-day Schengen limit, and a Schengen visa or stay does not entitle you to enter Ireland. If you arrive via Northern Ireland you must still report to an Immigration Officer within 30 days (7 days if for business or employment).

Boarding card

Useful at the border if asked: travel itinerary, proof of sufficient funds, health/travel insurance covering your stay, accommodation details, and any invitation or letter explaining the purpose of your visit
notes: INIS's visa-waiver page states (Note 3): "As per the Minister for Justice's announcement on 25 February 2022, citizens of Ukraine do not need a visa to travel to Ireland." This is a ministerial waiver introduced at the start of the war rather than a long-standing visa exemption, so confirm with INIS that it is still in force before you travel. No visa or pre-clearance is needed while it applies. Ireland has no ETA-style pre-travel authorisation. On arrival by air or sea from outside the State you must present to an Immigration Officer, who decides how long you may stay — INIS: "up to a maximum of 3 months" — and stamps your passport; the officer can still refuse entry if not satisfied by your documents or explanations. Staying beyond 90 days requires applying to Immigration Service Delivery for permission. Ireland is not in Schengen: days here do not count toward the 90/180-day Schengen limit, and a Schengen visa or stay does not entitle you to enter Ireland. If you arrive via Northern Ireland you must still report to an Immigration Officer within 30 days (7 days if for business or employment).

legal_source.name: Immigration Service Delivery (Ireland) — Visa & Non-Visa Required Nationalities

documentsNeeded: Irish short-stay 'C' visa obtained before travel (applied for online via INIS AVATS) or a valid UK short-stay visitor visa under the visa-waiver arrangements described in the notes
Valid passport
Boarding card
Supporting documents for the Immigration Officer: proof of funds, accommodation details, itinerary, insurance and the visa application papers
notes: Chinese (People's Republic of China) nationals are on Ireland's visa-required list (official INIS table). Two routes exist: (1) apply for an Irish short-stay visa (a 'C' visa is valid for up to 3 months per Citizens Information; the Immigration Officer still decides admission and length of stay, up to 90 days); or (2) if you are living in China you may use the British Irish Visa Scheme / Short Stay Visa Waiver Programme: a UK short-stay visitor visa lets you visit Ireland without a separate Irish visa, but only if you have first landed and gained lawful entry to the UK on that visa (each separate UK leave period, up to 180 days, needs a fresh UK entry before travelling to Ireland). Visas endorsed 'BIVS' must be used in the issuing country first. A visa never guarantees entry. The Hong Kong and Macau SARs are on the non-visa list; this row applies to People's Republic of China passport holders generally.

documentsNeeded: Valid Chinese passport (regular passport holders)
Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) — required of most foreign visitors, submitted online within 3 days before arrival
A visa in advance if the purpose is work, study, media work, or any activity requiring special approval, or a stay over 30 days
notes: Under the Malaysia–China mutual visa exemption in force from 17 July 2025, Chinese regular-passport holders may enter for up to 30 days per entry, and no more than 90 days in total in any 180-day period, for tourism, visiting family and friends, business, cultural exchange, medical treatment and personal affairs. Reported by Malaysia's state broadcaster RTM citing the announcement; Malaysia's Immigration Department FAQ page could not be read directly. The end date of the arrangement was not confirmed from a primary source — check the Immigration Department before booking far ahead.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport
Sufficient funds to stay in Georgia and to return home
Health and accident insurance (the border can refuse entry without either)
notes: The United States is on Georgia's visa-free list. Note 1 to Government Ordinance No. 255 says citizens of listed countries "may enter and stay in Georgia without visa for one full year" — the data uses 365 days; it is commonly described as 360 days in practice, so don't plan to the last day. Under the Law on the Legal Status of Aliens, Art. 11(1)(d), entry may be refused if a traveller lacks sufficient funds to stay and return or health and accident insurance. There is no arrival card and no return ticket is formally required by that law.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport (valid at least 3 months beyond the requested visa period, with at least 2 blank pages)
Georgian e-visa — OR a valid visa/residence permit from a country on Ordinance No. 256's list (see notes) for visa-free entry
Passport-style photo taken within the last 6 months (e-visa)
Travel/health insurance
Proof of accommodation for the whole stay
Proof of sufficient funds
notes: Chile does not appear on Georgia's visa-free list (Ordinance No. 255 and the Georgian National Tourism Administration's list agree), so Chilean citizens need a visa. Two routes: (1) the e-visa at evisa.gov.ge for short stays — "20 USD + 2% service fee", and "not less than 5 working days" to decide; the validity/stay varies by passport country (the portal cites 120/30 and 180/90 formats), so confirm Chile's figures in the application; or (2) visa-free entry for 90 calendar days in any 180-day period if you hold a valid visa or residence permit from a country on Ordinance No. 256's list (which includes the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Israel, Ireland, the GCC states and most EU/EEA states) — it must be valid on the day you cross the border.

documentsNeeded: Passport with a machine-readable zone; UK FCDO advises it must expire at least one month after arrival (an older Maldives consulate page says six months — carrying six months is the safe choice)
Return or onward ticket out of the Maldives
Confirmed resort/hotel booking, or enough funds to cover the stay (the Maldives consulate page cites US$100 plus US$50 per day)
IMUGA Traveller Declaration, submitted free of charge within 96 hours before your flight arrives (imuga.immigration.gov.mv)
notes: A free 30-day tourist visa is issued on arrival to bona-fide visitors of all nationalities except Israeli passport holders, who are barred from entry. The full 30 days is at the immigration officer's discretion, not a right; working on a tourist visa is prohibited and can lead to removal. An older Maldives consulate page describes extensions of up to a further 60 days for a fee (verify current terms with Maldives Immigration). Only use the official IMUGA portal for the declaration — it is free.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 3 months after your planned departure from Albania and issued within the last 10 years
Return/onward ticket (may be requested)
Confirmation of accommodation (may be requested)

notes: The U.S. Embassy in Tirana states directly: "U.S. citizens do not need a visa to enter the Republic of Albania; U.S. citizens generally are allowed to stay in Albania for up to one year without a residence permit." This is a long-standing bilateral arrangement, far more generous than the 90/180-day rule most other nationalities get. To "restart the clock" on the one-year limit you must leave Albania and stay out for at least 90 days; shorter trips abroad do not reset it. Staying beyond one year, taking a job, or enrolling in school requires a residence permit. Passport validity: Albania's own visa rules for foreigners (Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, "Regjimi i vizave për të huajt", section II: https://punetejashtme.gov.al/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/II-NR.3-REGJIMI-I-VIZAVE-PER-TE-HUAJT-INFO-PER-TE-HUAJT.pdf, checked 2026-10-18) require at least 3 months after the date you leave, and issue within the last 10 years. The U.S. Embassy says "at least three months of remaining validity" and recommends six months from your planned departure.

Passport valid for at least six months beyond your planned arrival date, with at least one blank page
Selfie or passport-type photo
Accommodation booking confirmation and arrival/departure itinerary

Kenyan Government travel health insurance (mandatory from 5 October 2026 for most visitors staying under 12 months): bought as part of the eTA application, or through the eCitizen insurance portal if you already hold an eTA; foreign travel insurance doesn't replace it. It is valid for 90 days, for multiple entries.
notes: The Netherlands is not on either of Kenya's eTA-exemption lists (the 90-day and 60-day national lists under the Kenya Citizenship and Immigration (Amendment) Rules, 2025, as reproduced on etakenya.go.ke's How to Apply page, checked 2026-10-02), so Dutch nationals need an approved eTA before travel. The eTA is valid for travel within 90 days of issuance; "once you arrive, the duration of your stay is determined at the point of entry" — no fixed number of days is guaranteed, so none is shown. The Standard (single-entry) eTA is listed at USD 30 on the official eligibility page; a One Year Multi-Entry eTA is listed at USD 300.

documentsNeeded: Approved Nigeria e-Visa (Tourism Visa – F5A) obtained online before travel, or an embassy-issued visa
Passport valid for at least 6 months
Passport-size photo
Evidence of return ticket
Evidence of hotel reservation or host address in Nigeria
Evidence of sufficient funds (180-day bank statement)
notes: The Nigeria Immigration Service states the Tourism Visa (F5A) is for "citizens of all countries except ECOWAS member States and other countries which Nigeria has entered into visa abolition/waiver agreements". The Netherlands is not an ECOWAS member, and no primary source found in this pass names it as having a visa-waiver agreement with Nigeria for ordinary passports (NIS publishes no such list). F5A terms (checked 2026-10-02): validity 90 days from issuance, single entry, stay of 30 days, not extendable, no employment. Fees were not verified — confirm on the official e-Visa portal (evisa.immigration.gov.ng).

documentsNeeded: Valid passport

notes: Rwanda's DGIE grants visa on arrival to citizens of all countries (since 1 Jan 2018). documentsNeeded: Valid passport
notes: Code 4 in Brazil's current QGRV (26 Aug 2026): visa exemption for up to 90 days (no 90/180 marker). Counting: Brazil's Decreto 9.199/2017 (art. 20 §1, applicable to visa-exempt visitors under art. 23) counts a visitor's stay from the first entry and pauses it while you are outside Brazil, so days add up across visits within a 12-month 'migratory year' starting at your first entry; the Federal Police may extend the stay by up to 90 days, to a maximum of 180 days per migratory year (https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_ato2015-2018/2017/decreto/d9199.htm). We show the stricter limit of 90 days in any 365 so a plan that fits here also fits the rule — check with the Federal Police if you need longer.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for the whole stay (French, Spanish and Italian foreign ministries advise at least 6 months' validity from entry)

notes: French ordinary-passport holders are on Thailand's 30-day visa-exemption list (60 countries/territories, EU listed as a bloc) that replaced the former 60-day scheme from 15 September 2026, after Ministry of Interior notifications were published in the Royal Gazette on 31 August 2026 (Gazette site itself not reachable for automated checks). Tourism only — other purposes need a visa. An extension of up to 30 days may be requested from the Immigration Bureau (Royal Thai Embassy London). People who entered under the old 60-day scheme before 15 September 2026 keep the stay they were granted. Cross-checked: the French MFA (diplomatie.gouv.fr, updated 15 Sep 2026) confirms the 30-day limit from 15 September 2026.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for not less than 6 months from the date of arrival in Sri Lanka
Approved Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) obtained before arrival (keeping a copy of the ETA approval notice is advised)
Confirmed return ticket
Sufficient funds to meet expenses during the stay
notes: Sri Lanka requires an ETA for all foreign visitors. United States ('UNITED STATES OF AMERICA') is one of the 40 countries whose nationals, with effect from 25.05.2026, 'are eligible to obtain tourist visa (ETA) free-of-charge for a period of 30 days' (diplomatic, official, service and ordinary passports). ETA fees paid before 25.05.2026 are non-refundable. The ETA gives a 30-day tourist visa with double entry: the second entry must fall within the 30 days from first arrival, and only the balance of those 30 days is granted on the second visit. Extension: the DI&E 'How to Extend Short Visit ETA' page says a short visit visa can be extended up to a maximum of 270 days from arrival (30 days on entry, 60 days at the first extension, 90 days at the second and third), applied for at the Visa Section of the Department of Immigration & Emigration head office (Battaramulla) or via the online e-Visa Extension portal (eservices.immigration.gov.lk) 'for extension up to 6 months'; the 'How to submit an ETA application' page instead says the ETA 'can be extended for up to six months' — the two DI&E pages conflict, so the safe reading is up to 6 months unless the department confirms more. Extension fees are charged even for holders of a free ETA. Other ETA rules from DI&E: an ETA holder must enter within three months of the ETA's issue (the FAQ separately says an ETA 'is valid for six months' — a conflict on the same site); you cannot obtain a fresh ETA while inside Sri Lanka; fees are non-refundable. A visa on arrival is also listed in the fee table (US$60 tourist for non-South-Asian nationals), but DI&E states all foreign nationals 'are required to obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) prior to their arrival', so apply in advance. Beware lookalike paid ETA sites — the only official portal is eta.gov.lk. Children under 12 of any nationality get a free 30-day tourist ETA. Documents and extension rules are from the same eta.gov.lk site: visainfo/apply.jsp (port-of-entry requirements), visainfo/extsheta.jsp (extensions), visainfo/center.jsp and visainfo/faq.jsp.

documentsNeeded: Ordinary passport valid for at least 6 months from the date of entry to Peru
Entry is recorded digitally at international airports (virtual Tarjeta Andina de Migración, TAM); if entering by land, make sure your passport is stamped
Immigration/customs may ask for a return or onward ticket, accommodation details and proof of sufficient funds
notes: United States ordinary passport holders are visa-exempt for tourism in Peru (Peru's Foreign Ministry table, PDF dated 16 Jul 2026, legal basis D.S. N° 23-95-RE). The table marks the tourist term as '90*', defined as '90 days, extendable once for an equal period, within a period of 365 days counted from the first entry into national territory'. So the automatic allowance is 90 days, and one extension of up to 90 more days (180 total) within the 365 days that start on your first entry is possible; we model the stricter 90 days per 365-day window. The extension is applied for with Migraciones while your stay is still valid; we did not find a current Migraciones page giving the fee and procedure for non-Andean tourists, so check with Migraciones. Business visits that are not visa-exempt in the table need a business visa. Passport validity: the Embassy of Peru in Singapore's visa FAQ (gob.pe, 22 Mar 2026) says the passport 'must have a minimum of 6 months validity from the date of entry to Peru'; the UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada travel advice say the same. Air arrivals are not stamped; Migraciones records entry digitally (virtual TAM) and you can check your authorised stay online at Migraciones; land arrivals must get an entry stamp (FCDO, Global Affairs Canada). Global Affairs Canada says officials may ask for a return/onward ticket, proof of accommodation and proof of funds, and that overstaying incurs a fine for each day, payable on exit. Law: Decreto Legislativo 1350 (Migraciones) as amended by D.Leg. 1582 (El Peruano) sets the tourist stay at 'up to 183 calendar days, cumulative over a 365-day period counted from the first regular entry', or the shorter term fixed in a visa-waiver agreement; where less than 183 days is granted an extension can be granted up to that limit unless the agreement sets a lower term or forbids extension. Tourist status does not allow paid work.

notes: The Dominican Foreign Ministry (MIREX) visa-requirements tool, queried for United States / ordinary passport / tourist visa (TS), answers '¿Requiere visa? NO'. UK and Canadian government advice both say tourists can visit visa-free for up to 30 days. Stay: the Dirección General de Migración (DGM) service page 'Prórroga de estadía para turistas' (migracion.gob.do/servicio/prorroga-de-estadia/) says tourists are allowed '30 días establecidos para los turistas' and that a stay of more than 30 days can be authorised 'a través de una prórroga extensible hasta 120 días'. Extension: apply online at the DGM portal (personal.migracion.gob.do / servicios.migracion.gob.do) with a copy of the passport data page, the stamp/date of last entry, a return air ticket, proof of own funds and a medical certificate; processing three working days; the application is free but the stay fee is charged: RD$3,500 for 30–90 days and RD$5,600 for 90–120 days, payable online or at the airport. Overstay: DGM's 'Servicio de cálculo y pago de tasas de estadía' says foreigners who exceed their authorised stay regularise it on departure by paying the stay fee (table: 30–90 days RD$3,500; 3–9 months RD$5,600; 9–12 months RD$7,000; rising to RD$98,000 for 10 years plus RD$7,000 per extra year), calculated at stayfee.migracion.gob.do. DGM's FAQ adds that if the stay fee is paid in advance at DGM you then have 30 days to leave. Canada's travel advice (travel.gc.ca, updated 26 May 2026) says to request the extension before the tourist card expires and that overstayers 'could be deported or refused re-entry'. Arrival form: DGM states the electronic E-Ticket (eticket.migracion.gob.do) is mandatory for every passenger on entry and on exit (combined migration and customs declaration, laws 285-04, 115-17, 72-02 and 226-06); UK advice says it can be completed up to 7 days before arrival and gives a QR code. Tourist card: the tax authority DGII says foreigners entering without a consular visa must have a Tourist Card (US$10, or €10 at sea/land ports only), with exemptions for nationals covered by bilateral agreements ratified by Congress; for air arrivals its cost is included in the airline ticket. The MIREX tool does not say whether this nationality is card-exempt. UK and Canadian advice both say you may be asked for proof of onward/return travel; Canada adds proof of adequate funds and your address in the country. Passport: under DGM's measure announced 2 December 2025 (memorandum continuing Resolución DGM-01-2024 of 31 May 2024), citizens of Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, the USA, 'Inglaterra' and EU countries travelling exclusively for tourism need a passport valid only for the length of their stay and departure, instead of the 6-month minimum 'que usualmente se exige'. This applies from 1 Dec 2025 to 31 Dec 2026 — re-check for travel in 2027.

legal_source.name: MIREX — Consulta de requisitos para extranjeros ingresar a la República Dominicana (Netherlands, pasaporte ordinario, Visa Turismo TS)

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for the whole stay
Onward or return ticket (may be requested at the border)
Proof of sufficient funds (may be requested at the border)
notes: Visa-free: 'Estados Unidos de América' is on the list in Art. 3 literal A of Resolución 5488 de 2022 (as modified by Res. 8558 de 2025), whose holders may 'ingresar, permanecer y salir de Colombia, exentos de requisito de visa' for airport transit or short-stay activities (short stay defined as under 90 days, extendable up to 180 days) that are not paid in Colombia. Colombian law: visitors from visa-exempt countries get a Permiso de Ingreso y Permanencia (PIP) at the border. A Tourism Permit (PT) is 'hasta por noventa (90) días calendario' per entry (Resolución 3167 de 2019 Art. 14, Migración Colombia). Migración Colombia counts each foreigner's days so they do not exceed 180 calendar days, continuous or discontinuous, in the same calendar year (1 Jan–31 Dec). Extension: the Permiso Temporal de Permanencia (PTP, 'prórroga') extends a Tourism Permit by up to 90 more calendar days, never beyond 180 days in the calendar year; apply online (Formulario Único de Trámites) at least 5 business days before the PIP expires; 2026 fee COP 150,000 (Resolución 0599 de 2026); issued by email 3 business days after payment; grant is discretionary. Modelled here as 180 days in any 365-day window, which is stricter than the legal calendar-year count (the legal rule would allow, e.g., 180 days ending 31 Dec and a new allowance from 1 Jan) — and each single entry is still capped at 90 days unless extended. Entry documents (Migración Colombia 'Requisitos de entrada y salida del país'): valid passport, plus 'tiquete de viaje de salida y demostrar solvencia económica, según corresponda'; officers may also ask for invitation letters or lodging (Res. 3167/2019 Art. 8 par. 2). Any paid activity requires a visa. Check-Mig online pre-registration (72 h to 1 h before travel) is free and explicitly 'no es de carácter obligatorio' per Migración Colombia. Conflict noted: gov.uk (FCDO, updated 2026-10-06) says visitors may extend 'by up to 120 days' and 'cannot remain ... more than 180 days in any 12-month period'; the Colombian sources (PTP page, Res. 3167/2019) say a 90-day PTP and 180 days per calendar year — the Colombian rule controls. Travel advice (gov.uk) adds: yellow-fever vaccination certificate required if arriving from certain countries with transmission risk; Colombian dual nationals must enter and leave on their Colombian document.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport (valid for the whole stay)
notes: Argentina's immigration authority (Dirección Nacional de Migraciones, DNM) lists no visa requirement for ordinary passports of this nationality in its 'Régimen de Visas' table (read 2026-10-09). Argentina's official tourist-entry page (argentina.gob.ar/migraciones/documentacion-para-ingresar-al-pais-como-turista) says tourists may stay 'hasta TRES (3) MESES PRORROGABLE POR OTRO PERÍODO SIMILAR' (up to 3 months, extendable once for a similar period) and may not do paid work; the Cancillería tourist-visa page and consulates express the tourist stay as 90 days, so it is modelled as 90 days per entry. Extension: request it from Migraciones before your permitted stay ends; no fee was stated on the pages read. Health insurance: Decreto 366/2025 (Boletín Oficial 29/05/2025) changed art. 34 of Migration Law 25.871 so that foreigners must present a sworn declaration of the purpose of entry and that they hold health insurance, but its new art. 123 bis says that declaration 'será exigible una vez reglamentada su implementación' (only enforceable once regulated); no implementing regulation was found as of 2026-10-09, so it is not listed as a required document. Outside emergencies, national public hospitals may charge foreigners without permanent residence (new art. 8), so insurance is strongly advisable. Cross-check not possible: travel.state.gov was blocked (Cloudflare) from this environment; status rests on the DNM table.

notes: Permitted length of stay is not stated by any Jordanian authority we could read: the Ministry of Interior's fee table lists visa VALIDITY tiers (3 months single entry JOD 40, 3 months double JOD 60, 6 months multiple JOD 120, 1 year, 5 years), not a stay length, and traveller governments disagree (Japan MOFA: 90-day stay permit; UK: visa 'valid for 3 months'; France and Spain: 1 month). We therefore show no day count — the stay is whatever your visa states; confirm at the border. UK FCDO: 'You can buy a single-entry visit visa when you arrive at a Jordanian airport or the Sheikh Hussein/North Border land crossing. It costs 40 Jordanian dinars (JOD) and is valid for 3 months.' Extension online 'for up to 6 months'; overstaying can be fined. Non-tourism visits (work, study) need a visa in advance online. documentsNeeded: Valid machine-readable passport (valid at least 1 day on entry; your stay cannot exceed its expiry)
Return or onward ticket (or navigation plan naming the destination port)
Proof of funds: at least US$100 per month or part-month of stay
Customs traveller declaration (Declaración de Viajero) on arrival
notes: Costa Rica's current visa directive (AJ-484-11-2025, in force since publication 17 Nov 2025; it repealed the Oct 2023 directive DG-30-10-2023-AJ) lists the United States (and its dependencies: Guam, US Virgin Islands, American Samoa, US Minor Outlying Islands; Puerto Rico is listed separately) in the FIRST GROUP: 'INGRESO SIN VISA. PERMANENCIA MÁXIMA: HASTA 180 DÍAS NATURALES NO PRORROGABLES. (Únicamente se prorrogará a quienes se le otorguen menos de 90 días y hasta por un máximo de 90 días). VIGENCIA MÍNIMA DE PASAPORTE: HASTA UN DÍA (el plazo de permanencia otorgado por el oficial de control migratorio, no será mayor al de la vigencia del pasaporte).' So: no visa; the border officer decides the stay, up to 180 calendar days counted from entry (per entry — the directive sets no cumulative cap across trips), and never beyond the passport's expiry; your passport only needs to be valid on the day of entry, but a longer validity buys a longer stay. The stay cannot be extended unless the officer granted fewer than 90 days, in which case an extension of up to 90 days can be requested (the text does not say whether 90 is the extra time or the total). Check the stamp: the days granted are what count, not the 180-day ceiling. Entry requirements for every foreigner (Directrices, PRIMERO §4, citing art. 42 Ley General de Migración y Extranjería 8764 and art. 30 Reglamento de Control Migratorio 36769-G): a valid, machine-readable/biometric passport in good condition; a visa where required; proof of funds of at least US$100 per month or part-month of authorised stay; a return or onward ticket (or a navigation plan naming the destination port); and no bar to entry. Tourist (No Residente, subcategoría Turismo) status allows leisure, business or professional activities only if they involve no pay or profit in Costa Rica. Also on arrival: a customs traveller declaration (Declaración de Viajero) is required of every arriving traveller (art. 368 Reglamento a la Ley General de Aduanas, Decreto 44051-H). Per the UK FCDO page (cross-check), a yellow fever vaccination certificate is required if you are coming from a country listed as a yellow-fever transmission risk, an air departure tax of US$29 may apply (usually included in the ticket), and overstayers can be fined US$100 per month and refused future entry; travel.gc.ca (updated 31 Aug 2026) adds that people deported for overstaying may be barred from re-entering for 5 to 10 years.

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 3 months on arrival (MOI). Note: GOV.UK, Auswärtiges Amt, France Diplomatie, Canada and NZ advise at least 6 months — carry 6 months to be safe with airlines
Confirmed return or onward ticket
Confirmed hotel reservation in Qatar for the visit, or a clear address of a friend/relative where you will stay

Health insurance from an insurance company accredited by Qatar's Ministry of Public Health (MOI lists it as a condition of the on-arrival visa; GOV.UK/Auswärtiges Amt describe it as mandatory for stays over 30 days)
notes: Qatar MOI page 'Free On-arrival Tourist Visa for 90 Days Non-extendable for (43) Countries' lists France. Conditions: '1- Passport valid for at least three months 2- Availability of confirmed return ticket 3- Hotel reservation at any hotel in Qatar during the visit period, or a clear address of a friend or relative. 4- Health insurance from an accredited insurance company.' The stay is free of charge and NOT extendable. The Auswärtiges Amt (Germany, Stand 09.10.2026) describes this same waiver as valid for 180 days from issue, multiple entry, allowing at most 90 days of stay within that validity, and Nederland Wereldwijd says 'maximaal 90 dagen binnen 180 dagen'. Modelled as a rolling 90-days-in-180 window, the stricter representation of '90 days within a 180-day validity period'. France Diplomatie (15 Sep 2026): 'Pour les courts séjours d'une durée inférieure à 90 jours, les ressortissants français sont dispensés de visa'; return/onward ticket and proof of accommodation required; insurance compulsory for stays over 30 days. Conflict noted: MOI requires passport validity of 3 months, but several travellers' governments (GOV.UK, Auswärtiges Amt, France, Canada, NZ) say 6 months; MOI is the controlling authority, documentsNeeded flags both. Health insurance: MOI lists 'Health insurance from an accredited insurance company' as a condition of every on-arrival category and its Entry Permits page says 'A valid health insurance policy from insurance companies registered with the Ministry of Public Health is required to enter Qatar', while GOV.UK and Auswärtiges Amt say it is compulsory for stays over 30 days (GOV.UK: standard premium QAR 50 per person per month). VisitQatar notes 'Visa-free entry is now the new term defining previously visa on arrival. Nothing changed except the name.' Entry is at the discretion of the border officer.

documentsNeeded: Passport issued within the last 10 years and valid for at least 3 months after your planned departure from Montenegro
Proof of the purpose of your stay and sufficient funds for the stay and your return or onward journey (may be requested at the border)
Registration of your stay with the police within 24 hours of arrival at each place of stay (hotels/accommodation providers usually do this for you)
notes: The Government of Montenegro (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) page for United States of America states that nationals of the United States of America 'may enter, pass through the territory of and stay in Montenegro up to 90 days, with a valid travel document, without a visa.' Law on Foreigners (Zakon o strancima, Official Gazette of Montenegro 12/18), Art. 34: a foreigner may stay in Montenegro 'najduže 90 dana u vremenskom periodu od 180 dana, računajući od dana prvog ulaska' (at most 90 days within a 180-day period, counted from the day of first entry), and may re-enter only after that 180-day period has passed; Art. 8 refuses entry to anyone who 'je već boravio 90 dana u periodu od 180 dana'. The law counts the 180-day period from the first entry rather than as a strictly rolling window; we model it as a rolling 90/180 window, which is the stricter reading (it never allows more days than the first-entry reading does). The UK FCDO page also states 'up to 90 days in any 180-day period'. Passport: Art. 9 of the Law on Foreigners treats a foreign passport as valid only if it was 'issued in the last ten years' and will not expire for at least three months after the planned departure from Montenegro. Art. 8 also allows entry to be refused if you cannot show the purpose and conditions of your stay or have insufficient means of subsistence for the stay and the return or onward journey. Registration: Art. 96 requires a foreigner staying up to 90 days to register their stay with the police within 24 hours of arriving at each place of stay (and to deregister within 24 hours before leaving); hotels and accommodation providers register guests (Art. 101: within 12 hours), and in private accommodation you can register through the local tourist organisation free of charge. FCDO warns failure to register can lead to a fine, detention or a court appearance. Montenegro is not in the Schengen Area, so days here and in Schengen are counted separately. Staying longer than 90 days needs a long-stay (D) visa or residence permit.

Registration of your stay with the police within 24 hours of arrival at each place of stay (hotels/accommodation providers usually do this for you)
notes: The Government of Montenegro (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) page for United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland states that nationals of the United Kingdom 'may enter, pass through the territory of and stay in Montenegro up to 90 days, with a valid travel document, without a visa.' This also covers holders of valid travel documents issued in the British Overseas Territories listed on the page. Law on Foreigners (Zakon o strancima, Official Gazette of Montenegro 12/18), Art. 34: a foreigner may stay in Montenegro 'najduže 90 dana u vremenskom periodu od 180 dana, računajući od dana prvog ulaska' (at most 90 days within a 180-day period, counted from the day of first entry), and may re-enter only after that 180-day period has passed; Art. 8 refuses entry to anyone who 'je već boravio 90 dana u periodu od 180 dana'. The law counts the 180-day period from the first entry rather than as a strictly rolling window; we model it as a rolling 90/180 window, which is the stricter reading (it never allows more days than the first-entry reading does). The UK FCDO page also states 'up to 90 days in any 180-day period'. Passport: Art. 9 of the Law on Foreigners treats a foreign passport as valid only if it was 'issued in the last ten years' and will not expire for at least three months after the planned departure from Montenegro. Art. 8 also allows entry to be refused if you cannot show the purpose and conditions of your stay or have insufficient means of subsistence for the stay and the return or onward journey. Registration: Art. 96 requires a foreigner staying up to 90 days to register their stay with the police within 24 hours of arriving at each place of stay (and to deregister within 24 hours before leaving); hotels and accommodation providers register guests (Art. 101: within 12 hours), and in private accommodation you can register through the local tourist organisation free of charge. FCDO warns failure to register can lead to a fine, detention or a court appearance. Montenegro is not in the Schengen Area, so days here and in Schengen are counted separately. Staying longer than 90 days needs a long-stay (D) visa or residence permit.

documentsNeeded: Valid passport — the Embassy of Jamaica in Washington says it should have at least six months' validity (UK, Canadian, French and Spanish government advice say valid for the duration of the stay; the six-month figure is the stricter one)
Return or round-trip ticket to a country you are admissible to
Evidence of sufficient funds to support yourself during the stay
Completed Immigration/Customs C5 form (online at enterjamaica.gov.jm, run by PICA and Jamaica Customs, or on paper on arrival)
notes: Visa-free. The PICA Visa Unit country listing (13 March 2025) shows UNITED STATES OF AMERICA: 'NONE – 6 months'; PICA's web table: 'NO visa required for 6 months'. The source states 6 months, not a day count; 180 days is used here as a conservative stand-in (6 months is always at least 181 days), and the immigration officer may grant less — the date stamped in your passport governs. 6 months is also PICA's stated maximum visitor stay for non-Commonwealth citizens, so no further extension as a visitor should be expected. travel.state.gov could not be read (HTTP 403) for a US-government cross-check. Common to all visitors (Embassy of Jamaica, Washington, 'Requirements for entry into Jamaica', embwashington.mfaft.gov.jm/visitor_to_jamaica): national passport with 'at least six months' validity', a return or round-trip ticket, and 'evidence of sufficient funds'; 'the decision in respect of admission and length of stay in the country rests with the Immigration Officer' at the port of entry, so the date stamped in your passport is what counts. Every passenger completes the Immigration/Customs C5 card (PICA, 'Travel Documents Required': complete and sign the C5 online or on paper; the official online form is enterjamaica.gov.jm). Extension (PICA, 'Extension of Stay', pica.gov.jm/immigration/extension-of-stays): apply to PICA before your landing time expires; 'Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 12 months stay on the island' and 'Non-Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 6 months stay on the island as a visitor'; processed within three working days. PICA fee schedule (pica.gov.jm/immigration/fees, no effective date shown): extension of stay processing fee JM$10,000, and JM$50,000 for persons who wish to extend their stay beyond the visa-exemption period. Source dates: the March 2025 PICA PDF is the newest official country list found; PICA's own web table (pica.gov.jm/immigration/entry-visa-requirements) still says 'Last updated July 19, 2023'.

notes: Visa-free. Bahamas Immigration 'Entry Requirements': no visa for 'United States Citizens entering as a bona fide visitor for a stay not exceeding eight (8) months.' The source states 8 months, not days; we model 240 days, which is never longer than any 8-month span. The officer stamps the actual period, which may be shorter. US citizens are not exempt from the passport requirement ('Passports are required by all persons entering The Bahamas'). Bahamas Immigration 'Before Your Arrival' (updated 2026-08-10) sets the entry criteria under the Immigration Act (Ch. 191) s.22: a valid return ticket/means of departure, no intention to work, financial means (or a local sponsor), a passport valid for at least six months (passport cards not accepted) and a completed Disembarkation/Embarkation Card. 'Admittance is not automatic' — the officer can refuse leave to land. The officer also decides how long you may stay; the period is documented in your passport ('the maximum period of stay, documented in visitors' passports, may vary, as this is dependent upon the discretion of the immigration officer at the port of entry'), and the absolute maximum for a visitor is 8 months. Extensions: apply to the Department of Immigration before the granted time expires; in-person interview with an extension officer; $200.00 non-refundable processing fee since 18 September 2024; bring return ticket, valid passport, local address, the Immigration landing card, reason for extension, sponsor's passport and address (Immigration 'Extension of Stay' page). Overstaying is a punishable offence. Yellow fever certificate required from travellers over 1 year arriving from (or transiting more than 12 hours through) a listed risk country (including Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Kenya and others), vaccinated at least 10 days before entry.

Return ticket or other means of departing The Bahamas
Proof of sufficient funds for the stay (or a local sponsor who will receive you)
Completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card
Yellow fever vaccination certificate only if arriving from (or transiting >12 hours through) a country with yellow fever risk
notes: Stay length: Bahamas Immigration only says visa-exempt visitors may remain 'for a period not exceeding three (3) months or eight (8) months as each individual agreement may dictate', and the immigration officer stamps the actual period on arrival. No source states which applies to this passport, so we show no day count — check the date stamped in your passport. Visa-free. Bahamas Immigration lists this nationality among those whose 'Bahamian visa requirements are waived ... to visit and remain in The Bahamas for a period not exceeding three (3) months or eight (8) months as each individual agreement may dictate', and advises 'all visitors intending to remain in The Bahamas for an excess of ninety (90) days [to] review the visa requirement for their specific country.' The specific agreement for this nationality (3 vs 8 months) is not published, so we model 90 days (the source states '3 months'; 90 used as the safe figure) — the period stamped in your passport by the officer is what counts. Also on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs 'Who DOES NOT need a visa to enter The Bahamas' list (modified 2026-03-03). Bahamas Immigration 'Before Your Arrival' (updated 2026-08-10) sets the entry criteria under the Immigration Act (Ch. 191) s.22: a valid return ticket/means of departure, no intention to work, financial means (or a local sponsor), a passport valid for at least six months (passport cards not accepted) and a completed Disembarkation/Embarkation Card. 'Admittance is not automatic' — the officer can refuse leave to land. The officer also decides how long you may stay; the period is documented in your passport ('the maximum period of stay, documented in visitors' passports, may vary, as this is dependent upon the discretion of the immigration officer at the port of entry'), and the absolute maximum for a visitor is 8 months. Extensions: apply to the Department of Immigration before the granted time expires; in-person interview with an extension officer; $200.00 non-refundable processing fee since 18 September 2024; bring return ticket, valid passport, local address, the Immigration landing card, reason for extension, sponsor's passport and address (Immigration 'Extension of Stay' page). Overstaying is a punishable offence. Yellow fever certificate required from travellers over 1 year arriving from (or transiting more than 12 hours through) a listed risk country (including Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Kenya and others), vaccinated at least 10 days before entry.

legal_source.name: Nederland Wereldwijd — Reisadvies Bahama's (Paspoort, visum; updated 7 Oct 2026)

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least 6 months (UK FCDO: from arrival; Canada: beyond your planned departure)
Entry stamp / authorised-stay record from migration control on arrival (keep it — needed when leaving)
notes: Visa-free: United States is not on Ecuador's official list of nationalities that must have a visa to enter (MREMH 'Países de Régimen Especial' list on gob.ec and Cancillería 'Lista de países que deben presentar visa al ingresar al Ecuador'). Under LOMH Art. 66(6), tourists who do not need a visa receive an 'autorización de permanencia' at the official migration control point. LOMH Art. 56 (as reformed 24-X-2025): 'El plazo de permanencia autorizado como turista será de hasta 90 días en el período de un año contado a partir del primer ingreso que marca el inicio de su año cronológico, prorrogable en territorio ecuatoriano, por una sola vez hasta por 90 dias continuos adicionales, previa solicitud y pago de la tarifa respectiva'. Counting: the year starts on your first entry (not 1 January); the 90 days are a total for that year, not per entry. We model it as 90 days in any 365-day window (stricter than the law, and without the optional extension). Extension (Ministerio del Interior, gob.ec 'Emisión de prórroga de autorización de permanencia en territorio para extranjeros', updated 2025-10-31): up to 90 extra days, apply online or at a Servicio de Apoyo Migratorio with a valid passport and the extension form; cost 'el equivalente a una tercera parte del Salario Básico Unificado en el Ecuador'. With the extension the yearly maximum is 180 days. Overstay (LOMH Art. 169, falta migratoria leve 2.b): a tourist who stays past the authorised 90 days without an extension, past 180 days with one, or past 180 days when admitted for 180, is fined one 'remuneración básica unificada' (one Ecuadorian basic monthly wage). Health insurance: since the 2021 reform the LOMH (Art. 52) only says residents must hold public or private health insurance; no general insurance requirement for mainland tourists appears in the consolidated law. Galápagos (per UK FCDO and Global Affairs Canada travel advice, not an Ecuadorian page we could load): tourists may stay up to 60 days (Canada: '60 days in a 1-year period'); you need a Transit Control Card bought at Quito or Guayaquil airport before check-in, a return ticket to the mainland, proof of a hotel booking or host invitation, and (UK) travel health insurance. The Galápagos national-park entry fee is not stated here because no official Ecuadorian source for it could be loaded. Land arrivals: Global Affairs Canada (updated 2026-10-09) says travellers entering by land or river must present an apostilled criminal-record check covering the past five years (with a Spanish translation); minors travelling with family are generally exempt. Customs: you must file the online Formulario de Registro Aduanero (FRA) only if you bring taxable goods or USD 10,000+ in cash/bearer instruments (SENAE).

documentsNeeded: Ordinary (single-entry) visa — USD 50, online e-visa (recommended) or on arrival
Passport valid at least 6 months, with at least one unused visa page
Return ticket (must be shown at the point of entry)
Mandatory Tanzanian inbound travel insurance (NIC for mainland entry, ZIC for entry via Zanzibar)
Yellow fever vaccination certificate if arriving from or transiting a yellow-fever country
notes: United Kingdom is a Commonwealth country but is expressly excluded from the Commonwealth visa exemption ("Commonwealth countries except the United Kingdom, Canada, India, Pakistan, Australia and New Zealand"). UK FCDO advice adds that a multiple-entry visa cannot be obtained on arrival and visas are no longer issued by the Tanzanian High Commission in London. United Kingdom appears on Tanzania Immigration's list of "Countries whose nationals can obtain a visa upon arrival" — eligible for "both the online and the on arrival Visa facility"; Immigration recommends applying online at visa.immigration.go.tz (processed within ten days). Tourists need an Ordinary (single-entry) Visa, USD 50, non-refundable. Stay: the guidelines give the Ordinary Visa "a validity of up to 90 days" (a validity figure); Canada's official travel advice (updated 7 Oct 2026) describes it as a "3-month tourist ... single entry visa on arrival" and says stays over 90 days require applying for an eVisa in advance — so 90 days is used here. Holders who visit other East African countries may re-enter on the same visa while it is still valid. No work or business allowed. A visa grant is not a final authority to enter; the officer at the border may refuse entry. One visa covers both Mainland and Zanzibar. Mandatory inbound travel insurance: NIC's official FAQ states the cover "is mandatory to all foreigners traveling in Tanzania Mainland", entering by land, sea or air, premium the TZS equivalent of USD 44 per person, valid 92 days with multiple entries, buy online at inbound.nicinsurance.co.tz or at the entry point; residents of EAC/SADC partner states are excluded (https://inbound.nicinsurance.co.tz/faqs). Canada's travel advice (updated 7 Oct 2026) confirms the insurer is NIC for mainland entry and the Zanzibar Insurance Corporation (ZIC) for entry via Zanzibar. Yellow fever: Immigration's tourist-info page says visitors must follow the Ministry of Health's yellow fever requirements; Canada's advice says proof of vaccination is required if arriving from, or transiting an airport in, a yellow-fever country. Guidelines PDF dated September 2026 (immigration.go.tz upload of 2026-09-10).

documentsNeeded: Passport valid for at least three months from the date of arrival in Israel
Approved ETA-IL electronic travel authorisation obtained before departure (fee 25 NIS, non-refundable)
notes: Israel's Population and Immigration Authority (PIBA) lists United Kingdom as visa-exempt: the official ETA-IL eligibility checker, run on 2026-10-10 for a United Kingdom regular (national) passport with purpose 'Visit (Tourism)', returned 'Eligible — Based on your answers, you can apply for an ETA-IL' (the checker's country data also flags this nationality NEED_PERMIT=0). PIBA: 'As of January 1st, 2025, travelers to Israel must have a valid visa or ETA-IL approval before starting their journey.' An approved ETA-IL lets you travel to Israel and 'stay for up to 90 days per visit'; it is valid for up to 2 years or until the passport expires, whichever comes first, and a new one (another 25 NIS) is needed with a new passport or a change of name, gender or citizenship. Every traveller including minors needs their own ETA-IL (an adult applies for a minor). Replies usually come within 24–72 hours; PIBA recommends applying at least 72 hours before booking flights or hotels. Apply only on the official site israel-entry.piba.gov.il. An ETA-IL 'does not constitute a guarantee of entry' — a border control officer decides at arrival, and it can be revoked for immigration or security reasons. Not exempt: people with Israeli citizenship (including dual nationals travelling on a foreign passport — they must show proof of Israeli citizenship to the airline) or holders of a valid Israeli visa. Stays beyond 90 days need an extension request under PIBA procedures (no fee or maximum stated on the pages read). Work is not allowed on an ETA-IL.

Every traveller including minors needs their own ETA-IL (an adult applies for a minor). Replies usually come within 24–72 hours; PIBA recommends applying at least 72 hours before booking flights or hotels. Apply only on the official site israel-entry.piba.gov.il. An ETA-IL 'does not constitute a guarantee of entry' — a border control officer decides at arrival, and it can be revoked for immigration or security reasons. Not exempt: people with Israeli citizenship (including dual nationals travelling on a foreign passport — they must show proof of Israeli citizenship to the airline) or holders of a valid Israeli visa. Stays beyond 90 days need an extension request under PIBA procedures (no fee or maximum stated on the pages read). Work is not allowed on an ETA-IL.
